items.title: Anthropic CEO says AI backlash is 'fundamentally a crisis of trust'
items.note: TechCrunch covers Amodei's mid-August public response to investor Gavin Baker, where he pushed back on the claim that his warnings have been disproportionately negative and framed the AI backlash as a crisis of trust.

items.title: Megan Thee Stallion on Her Journey, Owning Her Power & What Act III Has In Store | IMO
items.note: New IMO episode released August 12, 2026, in which Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson talk with Megan Thee Stallion about fame, grief, social media boundaries and her upcoming album. One of the most covered IMO episodes of the summer.

items.title: Yvon Chouinard Was Destroying the Mountains He Loved. He Made 1 Painful Decision That Built the Patagonia Empire
items.note: Inc. piece published August 4, 2026 revisiting Chouinard's decision to abandon pitons, the environmental call that reshaped his business decades before sustainability became a buzzword. Part of a wave of coverage following the Dirtbag Billionaire biography.

items.title: World Premiere of Clarice Lispector's The Hour of the Star in Los Angeles
items.note: Brazilian actress Bruna Fachetti premiered a one-woman stage adaptation of Lispector's novella The Hour of the Star at The Broadwater in Los Angeles, running July 25 to August 1, 2026. Fachetti plays six characters, blending narration and performance.

items.title: Open-model AI is good competition for Anthropic and OpenAI
items.note: Washington Post op-ed where Gurley argues Chinese open-weight models are healthy free-market competition, not a security threat to ban. It ran July 20 and set off a week of open-source AI debate, picked up by Techmeme and RealClearMarkets.

items.title: All-In podcast host Chamath Palihapitiya on the current state of AI
items.note: CNBC Squawk Box appearance on July 14 in his new role as 8090 CEO, covering the AI capex boom and the IBM stock drop. His line that 'you're starting to see a little bit of the wheels come off' AI spending was widely quoted.

items.title: Leonencio Nossa lança biografia de Guimarães Rosa durante Semana Rosiana em Cordisburgo
items.note: Journalist Leonencio Nossa launched a 736-page biography of Guimarães Rosa on July 10, 2026, during the Semana Rosiana in Cordisburgo, published by Nova Fronteira and Topbooks. It draws on Itamaraty archives and nearly 2,000 of Rosa's letters, the fruit of two decades of research.

items.title: 38ª Semana Rosiana celebra os 70 anos de Grande Sertão: Veredas e Corpo de Baile
items.note: Cordisburgo, Rosa's birthplace in Minas Gerais, hosted the 38th Semana Rosiana on July 5 to 11, 2026, under the theme 'O sertão é do tamanho do mundo'. This edition marked 70 years since the 1956 publication of both Grande Sertão: Veredas and Corpo de Baile.

items.title: Se Eu Fosse Eu, Clarices
items.note: Stage production by ATA (Agrupação Teatral Amacaca) built from three Lispector stories, O Ovo e a Galinha, Miss Algrave and Perdoando Deus, which returned to Rio for a run at the Centro Cultural da Justiça Federal from July 3 to 26, 2026.

items.title: AI Sovereignty Wars, Palantir-Nvidia Deal, SCOTUS Birthright Ruling, Newsom's CA Budget Lie
items.note: Early-July All-In episode with Chamath in the host chair alongside Jason, Sacks and Friedberg, covering the Palantir-Nvidia open source deal and California's budget. Notable because he has since skipped some August episodes while running 8090 full time.

items.title: Live in the Future
items.note: Naval podcast episode from July 2 with Garry Tan (Y Combinator), Daniel Francis (Abel Police) and Farbood Nivi, on riding AGI, AI anxiety, defending Taiwan and the 'California Empire'. Includes 20 minutes of new material at the end.

items.title: Chamath Palihapitiya raises $135M Series A for his AI coding startup, takes CEO role
items.note: TechCrunch coverage of 8090 Labs closing a $135M Series A led by Salesforce Ventures, with Chamath taking the CEO seat, his first full-time operating role since Facebook. The company's Software Factory product targets enterprise AI-native software development.

items.title: Daniela Amodei Says Curiosity Is Underrated
items.note: Stanford GSB's View From The Top podcast episode, published June 29, 2026, recorded live with MBA student Gintare Zukauskaite. She covers her path from English literature to Anthropic, why she left OpenAI, and the tension between safety and revenue.

items.title: Ryuichi Sakamoto and Tin Drum: KAGAMI+
items.note: Japan premiere of the mixed-reality concert piece that captures Sakamoto's piano performance in three dimensions, running June 27 to October 12, 2026 at VS. in Umekita, Osaka with new staging. Currently on view.

items.title: Some U.S. Cities Solved Homelessness. The Rest Should Just Copy Them.
items.note: P3 Institute Substack post from June 23 arguing that a few cities have working homelessness playbooks and policy should copy what already works. Part of the open-research policy work Gurley now publishes under the P3 brand.

items.title: Leading for Tomorrow: Unlocking Human Potential in the Era of Continuous Change and Endless Possibility
items.note: New Wiley essay collection published June 22, 2026. Jennifer Aaker contributed a chapter, 'What Matters Now: Mortality, Meaning, and the Machine Age,' co-written with Sophie Hamilton.

items.title: Inside the Mind of Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei (The Circuit, extended interview)
items.note: Extended video interview with Emily Chang on Bloomberg's The Circuit, published June 17, 2026, going deep on how Amodei thinks about Anthropic's trajectory and AI risk.

items.title: Vastlands: The Crossing
items.note: Alison Entrekin's long-awaited English translation of Grande Sertão: Veredas, a decade in the making, published in June 2026 by Simon & Schuster in the US and Bloomsbury in the UK. The first new English version of Rosa's masterpiece since 1963, timed with the novel's 70th anniversary.

items.title: Ryuichi Sakamoto: seeing sound, hearing time at Hamburger Bahnhof
items.note: Berlin's Hamburger Bahnhof announced in June 2026 that the touring Sakamoto retrospective will open September 11, 2026 and run to May 23, 2027, his first major European retrospective, filling about 1,500 square meters of the Rieckhallen with five large-scale installations.

items.title: Policy on the AI Exponential
items.note: New essay on Amodei's personal site, published June 2026, arguing government should be able to block dangerous AI deployments. It reworks five policy areas for an AI world: safety regulation, macroeconomics and tax, science, state power, and geopolitics.

items.title: Get a Hobby, Be Happy with Jessica Williams
items.note: IMO episode released June 10, 2026, with actress Jessica Williams on being mentored by Jon Stewart at The Daily Show, navigating Hollywood as a tall Black woman, and the case for hobbies, plus stories from the set of Shrinking.

items.title: Anthropic President Amodei on the Future of Claude
items.note: Bloomberg Technology interview from early June 2026 where Daniela discusses where Claude is headed and Anthropic's enterprise growth.

items.title: The AI Industrial Revolution
items.note: Full Naval podcast episode from June 1 with Guillermo Rauch (Vercel), Blake Scholl (Boom Supersonic) and Max Hodak (Science), on software factories, vertical integration and the autonomous company. Ties directly into his current building phase at Impossible.

items.title: Ranking Venture Investors
items.note: New SSRN working paper by Ilya Strebulaev and Blake Jackson, posted May 26, 2026, building a ranking algorithm for VC firms and individual investors from 230,000-plus investments. Their top 100 overlaps with the Forbes Midas list on only 42 names.

items.title: 2026 CNBC Disruptor 50: Full interview with Anthropic co-founder Daniela Amodei
items.note: CNBC's Julia Boorstin interviews Daniela after Anthropic was named No. 1 on the 2026 Disruptor 50 list, on the company's growth and what comes next. Aired May 19, 2026.

items.title: Sell the Truth
items.note: A 28-minute Naval episode from May 11 on persuasion, credibility, charisma and knowing when to walk away from a deal. His core claim: figure out what you genuinely believe and say it as clearly as possible.

items.title: From Open Source Software to Open Source Strategy
items.note: A May 9 essay Gurley says he started writing three years ago, on how executives use open source to control standards and neutralize competitors, from GNU and Linux to today's AI and autonomous vehicle races. His first big post under the new P3 Institute brand.

items.title: A Conversation with Daniela Amodei, Co-Founder and President of Anthropic
items.note: Sixth Street podcast episode from May 2026 where Daniela talks through Anthropic's culture and strategy as the company scales.

items.title: Michelle Obama To Bring 'IMO: The Look' Live Conversation To 2026 ESSENCE Festival of Culture
items.note: Essence announced in May 2026 that Michelle Obama would open the Essence Festival Evening Concert Series on July 3 at the Caesars Superdome in New Orleans with a live IMO: The Look conversation, extending her book The Look into a live format.

items.title: An Ambitious Course on the Future of AI Ends with a Flourish
items.note: Stanford GSB piece from April 2026 on the final session of AI for Human Flourishing, the course Jennifer Aaker co-created with Fei-Fei Li. The 2026 cohort of 40 MBAs produced the first volume of a student anthology on flourishing in the AI era.

items.title: Covert Joy: Selected Stories
items.note: New Directions released the paperback edition of this selection of twenty Lispector stories in March 2026, translated by Katrina Dodson with an introduction by Rachel Kushner and a new preface by Lispector's son Paulo Gurgel Valente.

items.title: Ryuichi Sakamoto | seeing sound, hearing time at M+
items.note: M+ in Hong Kong presented the touring Sakamoto exhibition from February 14 to July 5, 2026, centered on the async immersion installation co-created with Shiro Takatani, plus Carsten Nicolai moving-image works paired with music from his final album 12. It closed in early July.

items.title: A rare interview with Yvon Chouinard
items.note: David Gelles, author of the Chouinard biography Dirtbag Billionaire, shares five takeaways from hours of conversation with the founder, including his admiration for the Henokiens club of 200-year-old companies, with video from a Copenhagen conference talk.

items.title: Dirtbag Billionaire: How Yvon Chouinard Built Patagonia, Made a Fortune, and Gave It All Away
items.note: David Gelles's biography of Chouinard, written with rare access including hiking in Wyoming and fishing in Argentina. It has driven most of the recent Chouinard press cycle, including a PBS NewsHour segment.
